key_insight: Syndrome records can be used in classical post-processing to virtually cancel logical errors in universal quantum circuits without needing prior noise learning or modified circuits.
engineering_relevance: This enables more practical logical-quantum mitigation workflows by reducing experiment complexity and bias in early fault-tolerant computations.
method: Use only measured syndrome records from the run.
Apply virtual error cancellation entirely in post-processing.
Pair a fast experimental decoder with a stronger decoder offline for a dual-decoder scheme.
evidence_signal: In simulations of a distance-7 rotated surface code, the dual-decoder method showed sample-size-dependent error reduction and achieved over three orders of magnitude suppression relative to the decoded logical error rate in an experimentally achievable setting.
watch_item: The approach still depends on decoder quality and may incur substantial classical post-processing and sampling overhead in practice.
paper_title: Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits
